questions.q: Why is a pipeline finishing with no exceptions not sufficient proof that its output is correct?
options: PySpark always raises an exception whenever a result is incorrect
Pipelines that finish without an error are mathematically guaranteed to be correct
This only applies to pandas pipelines, never PySpark ones
A bad join, an off-by-one filter, or a unit mix-up can all produce a result that looks plausible but is still wrong, with no error raised
questions.explain: This is the core reason validation checks exist separately from just watching for a crash.

questions.q: What does a row-count sanity check catch that a successful pipeline run might otherwise hide?
options: Syntax errors in the PySpark code
Whether the output file format is Parquet or CSV
Whether the SparkSession was created correctly
A filter upstream being too aggressive, or a join dropping far more rows than it should, without raising any error
questions.explain: A result with far fewer rows than expected is often the first visible symptom of an upstream bug.

questions.q: Why does finding a non-positive avg_fare in the validation step indicate a real bug?
options: Non-positive fares are expected and completely normal in this dataset
It only indicates a formatting issue, not a logic error
avg_fare is not derived from fare_amount at all
Lesson 47's clean() step should have already removed any fare of $0 or less before it reached the aggregation
questions.explain: If a non-positive average fare shows up here, the cleaning step upstream has a real bug that needs fixing.

questions.q: In the pytest fixture example, what does @pytest.fixture(scope="module") accomplish?
options: It is required for pytest to recognize any test function at all
It runs every test in a completely separate Python process
It loads the result DataFrame once and reuses it across all test functions in the file, instead of re-reading it every time
It deletes the result DataFrame after each individual test
questions.explain: scope="module" shares the fixture's return value across every test in that file rather than recreating it per test.

questions.q: Besides the raw numbers, what should a short write-up for the capstone include?
options: Only the PySpark code used to produce the result, with no plain-language explanation
Nothing else — the numbers alone are sufficient for any audience
A complete copy of the raw dataset
The business question, the real data source, the method used, and what validation was performed and passed
questions.explain: A write-up is what makes the result usable by someone who will never open the pipeline's code.
